answer: An AI-agent economy can deter Sybil attacks with time-domain reflectometry over copper links. Verifier switches send nanosecond pulses to record each port's impedance echo while the agent answers a cipher challenge directly on that wire. Because virtual clones behind one hub share a single echo, attackers must deploy separate cabling and transceivers per fake identity. Yet outdoor splices corrode, and a raven perching on an exposed span shifts capacitance and triggers false rejections.
